verdict: Gilead's revenue rose 7% to $8.3B as HIV sales jumped 18% — prevention sales nearly doubled — though profit fell to $2.4B because last year's quarter included a $569M other-income gain.

segments.name: HIV
segments.note: HIV treatment and prevention — Biktarvy alone was $4.1B (+10%), and prevention sales (including the long-acting Yeztugo rollout) nearly doubled.

segments.name: Liver Disease
segments.note: Hepatitis and liver-disease medicines, led by Livdelzi for primary biliary cholangitis.

segments.name: Oncology
segments.note: Cancer medicines including Trodelvy and cell therapies.

segments.name: Other products & royalties
segments.note: All other products — including Veklury (COVID antiviral) at $86M, down 69% — plus $11M of royalty, contract and other revenues.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Research and development across HIV, oncology, liver disease and inflammation programs.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Commercial teams and administration — up from $1,357M a year ago as launches expand.

opex.name: Acquired in-process R&D
opex.note: Up-front and milestone payments for research bought from partners, expensed immediately.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $269M plus $130M of other expense, net — a $399M drag. (A year ago this line was a $569M gain, which is why profit fell despite higher revenue.)
footerNote: Gilead does not print a gross-profit line; it reports total costs and expenses. The split here puts cost of goods sold ($1,571M) as the direct cost and its R&D, acquired in-process R&D and SG&A lines as running costs — the same total of $4,838M.

takeaways.title: HIV is growing again
takeaways.text: HIV product sales rose 18% to $6.25B: Biktarvy grew 10% to $4.1B and HIV prevention sales nearly doubled as long-acting prevention rolled out — the franchise is three-quarters of all product sales.

takeaways.title: EPS fell on a comparison quirk
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS fell to $1.94 from $2.43 even though operating income rose 4% — the year-ago quarter included $569M of other income (net) versus a $130M expense this year.

takeaways.title: Remember the first half
takeaways.text: Over the first nine months Gilead recorded $11.3B of acquired in-process R&D charges from buying research-stage assets, which is why its nine-month result is a $6.0B loss despite profitable quarters like this one.

oneTimers: Acquired in-process R&D expense was just $18M this quarter (versus $170M a year ago) — but the nine-month total is $11,307M, concentrated earlier in 2026.
SG&A rose 21% year over year to $1,641M as Gilead spends behind new launches in HIV and oncology.
